title: Performance fingerprint registry and staged canary rollout policy for verified profiles
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Teams onboarding models need a single authoritative performance artifact that describes latency P50/P95, throughput at common batch sizes, and cost-per-token under standard configs. Current verified profile publishing is ad-hoc and lacks a stable fingerprint and staged propagation plan, which makes rollouts risky for Dedicated/Private customers and causes regression incidents when runtime kernel changes interact with quantized variants.

Goal: Create a 'performance fingerprint' registry artifact (signed manifest) and a staged canary rollout policy that enables safe publishing and automatic rollback triggers. The registry should support: 1) per-model-version fingerprints with performance vectors for latency/throughput/cost and the test harness snapshot id; 2) signatures/timestamps for auditability; 3) propagation metadata (regions, deployment modes: hosted/dedicated/private, compatibility tags); 4) machine-readable gates consumed by the console and runtime to enforce pinning/rollbacks.

Scope: This ticket covers the product definition, acceptance criteria, and coordinated rollout plan with Eng and Console. Implementation details (API contract, storage) are in linked design doc and will be executed in ENG tickets after design sign-off.

Out of scope: model benchmarking harness changes (those are tracked separately), deep runtime rollback code (ENG will reference this artifact), and billing integration (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A signed performance fingerprint manifest format is defined and documented (JSON schema) including fields for model_version, latency_percentiles, throughput_at_batch_sizes, cost_estimates, harness_snapshot_id, supported_deployment_modes, and signature metadata.
Console UI shows per-model fingerprint with provenance (who published, when, linked benchmark run) and an explicit 'Promote to global' action that triggers staged propagation.

Publishing flow supports a staged canary propagation with three phases: staging (internal only), regional canary (10% of traffic in target region), and global promotion. Each phase must have observability gates (latency regressions, error-rate delta, cost variance) expressed as thresholds.
Automation hooks exist to trigger an immediate pause/rollback of propagation when a gate crosses threshold; hooks are wired to the rollout dashboard and to the runtime fallback policy.

Profile manifests are stored in the registry with an immutable history and can be pinned by customers to a specific manifest id or set to 'float within major' pin semantics. Pin and floating semantics are clearly documented.
Security and audit requirements satisfied: manifest signatures validated, publish actions logged, and security_review_required flagged in the release plan.

Review schema with Runtime and Bench teams (sync meeting)
